This Petition Is Coming On For Orders This Day, The
Court Made The Following:

 Nc: 2024:Khc-D:6949
 Wp No.102578 of 2024
 Order

Captioned petition is filed seeking following reliefs:
"1) Issue a writ of mandamus to the respondent No.1 to prepare the property data sheet giving the proper details and the dimensions of the actual of the schedule property of the petitioners and also nature of the property (residential/commercial).
Sri N Sivaramappa S/O ... vs National Highway Authroity Of India on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49849519/
6 2) Issue a writ of certiorari by quashing the data sheet prepared by the private agency on the order of first respondent authority produced as Annexure "B" series.
3) Pass such other orders as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit in the circumstances of the case, including the award of the costs of this petition, in the interest of justice and equity."
2. This Court bearing in mind that valuable rights of the land losers are involved was inclined to grant some protection vide order dated 24.04.2024.
3.
It is not in dispute that the petitioner's lands were acquired by the National Highways for the purpose of laying 4/6 leading up for Hospet - Bellary on National Highway No.63.
A notification was issued under Section 3A of the National Highways Act, 1956 (for short, 'the Act') thereby, proposing to acquire certain lands, which also included petitioner's property.

As per Section 3B of the Act, the SLAO along with Surveyor carried out a joint measurement of the acquired land and a final notification was issued on 19.04.2012 under Section 3D of NC: 2024:KHC-D:6949 the Act.
SLAO has passed an award on 28.10.2013 under Section 3G of the Act.
4. It is not in dispute that the petitioner/land losers have received compensation amount.

5. The petitioner's grievance before this Court is that the acquiring authority has not drawn a Mahazar and therefore, the same is detrimental to the petitioner's right to seek higher compensation under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956.
This contention is effectively rebutted by the standing counsel by filing the statement of objections.

6. If the acquisition proceedings are concluded and an award is passed in accordance with law and compensation is released to the land loser, petitioner cannot maintain the captioned writ petition seeking mandamus.
The petitioner has efficacious remedy under the Act.

If at all if he is aggrieved and award passed by the competent authority is not acceptable, without exhausting remedies provided under the Act, a mandamus cannot be sought against respondent No.1 to prepare a property data-sheet by furnishing proper details and dimensions of the suit schedule property.
The award admittedly NC: 2024:KHC-D:6949 contains particulars of the property acquired.
If petitioner is really aggrieved by the award and inadequacy relating to compensation, there is no impediment for petitioner to avail remedy under the Act.
The petitioner has no legal right to seek mandamus.
Correspondingly, respondent No.1 is not under obligation to prepare a property data-sheet, which is impermissible once award is passed.
Reserving liberty to the petitioner to avail remedy under the provisions of the Act, captioned writ petition stands disposed of.
All grounds urged in the writ petition are kept open.

opennyai_summary.facts: SLAO has passed an award on 28.10.2013 under Section 3G of the Act.
opennyai_summary.arguments: 5. The petitioner's grievance before this Court is that the acquiring authority has not drawn a Mahazar and therefore, the same is detrimental to the petitioner's right to seek higher compensation under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The petitioner has efficacious remedy under the Act.
If at all if he is aggrieved and award passed by the competent authority is not acceptable, without exhausting remedies provided under the Act, a mandamus cannot be sought against respondent No.1 to prepare a property data-sheet by furnishing proper details and dimensions of the suit schedule property.
If petitioner is really aggrieved by the award and inadequacy relating to compensation, there is no impediment for petitioner to avail remedy under the Act.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The petitioner has no legal right to seek mandamus.
Correspondingly, respondent No.1 is not under obligation to prepare a property data-sheet, which is impermissible once award is passed.
Reserving liberty to the petitioner to avail remedy under the provisions of the Act, captioned writ petition stands disposed of.
All grounds urged in the writ petition are kept open.
